title: Vireo after PR 178
eyebrow: Vireo engine · Windows (RTX 5060 Laptop, 8 GB) · 2026-11-15, night · main at b5ff3ae (PRs 173-178 merged) · four small models at Q4 · reading, writing and first token at four prompt sizes
headline: Within 5% of llama.cpp reading ~32K prompts, ahead on Gemma 4 E4B, level or ahead at the largest prompt on three of four
lede: The run after PRs 171 and 172 repeated on the merged build after PR 178, the same contexts and prompts, one run each through both servers with streaming. PR 177's one-kernel first half of the feed-forward and PR 178's DeltaNet scan on the tensor cores lift reading again: Vireo is {since:vireo|long.read_tps} faster on the ~32K prompt than after PR 172 and {since:vireo|xlarge.read_tps} on the largest, the Qwens the most, while llama.cpp, unchanged, moved {since:llama|long.read_tps} and {since:llama|xlarge.read_tps}. Against llama.cpp Vireo now reads the ~32K prompt {long.read_tps} (after PR 172: {old:long.read_tps}) and the largest prompts {xlarge.read_tps}. Writing is where it was: {medium.gen_tps} after ~3K tokens, {xlarge.gen_tps} after the largest prompt.

cards.text: Vireo reading the ~32K prompt against llama.cpp (after PR 172: {old:long.read_tps}); Vireo itself {since:vireo|long.read_tps} since, ahead on Gemma 4 E4B
reading the largest prompt each model fits on 8 GB; Qwen 3.5 4B ahead ({Qwen 3.5 4B|xlarge.read_tps}), Qwen 3.5 9B and Gemma 4 E4B level, Gemma 4 E2B behind

rig.label: Software
rig.detail: main with PRs 173-178 merged, cargo build --release · llama.cpp b12262 (CUDA build, -fa on, -ngl 99, -np 1) · vireo-server with --context and --thinking off

where: Small (a ~40-token question). Vireo first to the first token on the Gemmas and Qwen 3.5 4B ({Gemma 4 E2B|short.ttft}, {Gemma 4 E4B|short.ttft}, {Qwen 3.5 4B|short.ttft}); Qwen 3.5 9B's {Qwen 3.5 9B|short.ttft} is the main run's one-off below (re-checked at 94-103 ms against llama.cpp's 112). Times of 30-140 ms, so the percentages swing. Writing ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|short.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|short.gen_tps}, their draft models), level to a little behind on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|short.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|short.gen_tps}). Reading so few tokens is mostly fixed overhead and says little.

Medium (~3K tokens). Reading ahead on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|medium.read_tps}), level on Qwen 3.5 4B ({Qwen 3.5 4B|medium.read_tps}), behind on Qwen 3.5 9B ({Qwen 3.5 9B|medium.read_tps}); Gemma 4 E2B's {Gemma 4 E2B|medium.read_tps} is the first server's one-off again (drafting off it reads {plain:Gemma 4 E2B|medium.read_tps} against llama.cpp, re-checked +20%). Writing well ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|medium.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|medium.gen_tps}), level on the Qwens. First token {medium.ttft}.

Large (~32K tokens). Reading ahead on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|long.read_tps}), close behind on the rest: {Qwen 3.5 4B|long.read_tps} on Qwen 3.5 4B, {Gemma 4 E2B|long.read_tps} on Gemma 4 E2B, {Qwen 3.5 9B|long.read_tps} on Qwen 3.5 9B (after PR 172: {old:long.read_tps}); first token {long.ttft}. Writing ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|long.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|long.gen_tps}), behind on Qwen 3.5 4B ({Qwen 3.5 4B|long.gen_tps}), level on Qwen 3.5 9B ({Qwen 3.5 9B|long.gen_tps}).

Xlarge (the largest that fits). Reading ahead on Qwen 3.5 4B ({Qwen 3.5 4B|xlarge.read_tps}, first token too), level on Qwen 3.5 9B ({Qwen 3.5 9B|xlarge.read_tps}) and Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|xlarge.read_tps}), behind on Gemma 4 E2B ({Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.read_tps}). Writing behind on all four: {Gemma 4 E4B|xlarge.gen_tps} on Gemma 4 E4B, {Qwen 3.5 9B|xlarge.gen_tps} and {Qwen 3.5 4B|xlarge.gen_tps} on the Qwens, {Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.gen_tps} on Gemma 4 E2B (drafting off {plain:Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.gen_tps}).
method: Small, medium and large: evals/speed/bench-2026-11-13/bench.py with ENGINES=vireo,vireo-plain,llama MODELS=e2b,e4b,q4b,q9b REPS=1 WORK=short,medium,long and python -X utf8 -I, at 65,536 (32,768 for Qwen 3.5 9B). Xlarge: bench-2026-11-15-windows-after-pr178/xlarge.py (the after-PR-172 run's script, unchanged) at the same contexts, 131,072 for the Gemmas with all of xlarge.txt, 114,688 for Qwen 3.5 4B with it cut to 396,000 characters, 49,152 for Qwen 3.5 9B cut to 166,000, the same text for both engines; shared GPU memory read after loading and after the prompt. Each server warmed up with a five-word chat first; one server on the GPU at a time. Speeds are the servers' own (Vireo's log, llama.cpp's timings); first token is client-side. Every cell's change is against bench-2026-11-15-windows-after-pr172, the same workloads. Results: results.jsonl (48 rows), xlarge.jsonl (12), recheck-e2b-medium.jsonl, recheck-q9b-short.jsonl; page: evals/speed/bench_after_pr178_report.py.

notes.read_tps: Prompt tokens read ÷ the time reading them, as each server reports it. Vireo keeps its ~1,300 (Gemma) or ~1,480 (Qwen) tokens of instructions from the warm-up chat and does not read them again. Since after PR 172: Vireo {since:vireo|medium.read_tps} on ~3K, {since:vireo|long.read_tps} on ~32K and {since:vireo|xlarge.read_tps} on the largest; llama.cpp, unchanged, {since:llama|medium.read_tps}, {since:llama|long.read_tps} and {since:llama|xlarge.read_tps}.
notes.gen_tps: Vireo as shipped: the Gemmas with Google's draft models, both families with the chat's guesses, which stop for a reply when too few are taken deep in a chat. Answers differ in length between engines (the settings table has the counts); the large and xlarge answers are short (33-65 tokens), so those speeds are rougher. Since after PR 172 Vireo's writing moved {since:vireo|medium.gen_tps} on ~3K, {since:vireo|long.gen_tps} on ~32K and {since:vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} on the largest; llama.cpp {since:llama|medium.gen_tps}, {since:llama|long.gen_tps} and {since:llama|xlarge.gen_tps}.
notes.ttft: Seconds from sending the request to the first streamed token, on the client. Shown as llama.cpp ÷ Vireo − 1, so positive is Vireo quicker. The small prompt's first tokens take 30-140 ms on both engines, so their percentages and changes are noise-sized.
notes.plain: vireo-server with --mtp off --lookup 0: no draft model and no guesses, the same contexts and prompts. Bold is Vireo's writing speed with drafting off, then its difference from llama.cpp; under it, Vireo as shipped and how much drafting adds, and both settings' change since after PR 172. After ~125K tokens drafting costs Gemma 4 E2B {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps} tokens/s (after PR 172: {old:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {old:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps}) and Gemma 4 E4B little ({Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {Gemma 4 E4B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps}).
notes.settings: Context is the --context / -c each server ran with, the same for both engines in a row and the same as after PR 172. Prompt tokens are as each server counted them, with how many it kept from earlier (Vireo keeps its instructions; llama.cpp its ~24-token chat start). Shared GPU memory not growing between load and after the prompt is the check that nothing spilled into the PC's memory: it held on all twelve xlarge rows.
notes.probes: Not searched again: the contexts found after PR 169 (Qwen 3.5 4B spilled at 131,072, Qwen 3.5 9B at 57,344; xlarge-probes.jsonl there) were used as they were, and shared GPU memory stayed at its value at load on every server, 0.07 GB on Vireo and 0.16-0.24 GB on llama.cpp.

odd: Gemma 4 E2B as shipped read the ~3K prompt at {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|medium.read_tps} tokens/s in the main run, against {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|medium.read_tps} with drafting off: the fourth run in a row where the first server of the run reads this prompt low (15,315 after PR 172). Re-run alone afterwards, both settings, short, medium, short, medium (recheck-e2b-medium.jsonl): 19,131-19,150 every time, +19% to +20% against llama.cpp's {Gemma 4 E2B|llama|medium.read_tps}. The page keeps the main run's numbers.

Qwen 3.5 9B as shipped read the small prompt at {Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo|short.read_tps} tokens/s with its first token at {Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo|short.ttft} s and wrote {Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo|short.gen_tps}, against {Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo-plain|short.read_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo-plain|short.ttft} s and {Qwen 3.5 9B|vireo-plain|short.gen_tps} with drafting off. Re-run twice per setting (recheck-q9b-short.jsonl): 1,050-1,075 tokens/s, 93-103 ms, 56.4-56.7 tokens/s on both, so a one-off of an ~85-token prompt; the page keeps the main run's numbers.

Gemma 4 E4B's small prompt read at {Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|short.read_tps} tokens/s as shipped against {old:Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|short.read_tps} after PR 172 ({since:Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|short.read_tps}); 67 tokens in ~30 ms, noise at that size.

The first speed check before the run, right after the build, read at 5,908 tokens/s and wrote 82.9; the second and two more read 7,156-7,229 and wrote 87.0-87.8 (speed-check-before-repeat.txt), so the machine was at full speed.

llama.cpp, unchanged, landed within {llama_drift.max} of the after-PR-172 run on every medium, large and xlarge number (median {llama_drift.median}). The largest move was Gemma 4 E2B's first token on ~3K tokens (219 → 231 ms). Its small-prompt first tokens moved up to 38% (37 → 60 ms on Gemma 4 E2B): times that small are not comparable run to run.
Nothing errored, and no row spilled.
